title: In how many ways can twelve figs and seven figs make a rectangle?
description: Twelve figs and seven figs are laid in rows and columns, and every try that fills the rows exactly is kept. Twelve figs fit three rectangles and seven figs fit only one. Keeko doubts that seven figs can make a rectangle at all.
teaching_notes: One idea: a heap of figs makes a rectangle when the rows times the columns give the number of figs, and a single row counts too. Watch for students who say seven figs cannot make a rectangle.

source: {{NAME_1}} wants to put 12 figs in each box and {{NAME_3}} wants to put
video_script.why: The child finds every rectangular arrangement of twelve figs and of seven figs, and sees that twelve has more than one while seven has only the single row.
video_script.substitution: Try each number of rows and keep only the tries where the figs fill the rows exactly.
video_script.anchor: Figs from the farm of {{NAME_1}} and {{NAME_3}}, packed in boxes in rows and columns
video_script.wrong_answer: seven figs cannot make a rectangle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says seven figs cannot make a rectangle at all. One row of seven figs is a rectangle seven wide and one tall, so the doubt is crossed out.
video_script.payoff_line: Twelve figs make three rectangles, and seven figs make only one.

final_answer.spoken: twelve figs make three rectangles and seven figs make only one

names.{{NAME_1}}: packs twelve figs in each box
names.{{NAME_3}}: packs seven figs in each box

maths_rules: a rectangle of figs has the same number of figs in every row, so rows × columns = number of figs
5 rows of 2 figs use 10 figs and leave 12 - 10 = 2 over, so only exact fits count
7 figs: 7 × 1 = 7 only; 2 rows of 3 leave 1 over, 3 rows of 2 leave 1 over, 4 rows of 1 leave 3 over, 5 rows of 1 leave 2 over, 6 rows of 1 leave 1 over
slip: one row of 7 figs is a rectangle 7 wide and 1 tall
video_script.design: One heap of twelve figs and one heap of seven figs, laid in rows and columns on the same box; the rectangles that fit stay teal and the tries that leave figs over are crossed out.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; two empty boxes, one for each child; a card of twelve figs and a card of seven figs; the words how many arrangements

marks.farm: the two children appear beside a fig tree
marks.boxes: the cards of twelve figs and seven figs are placed on the two boxes
marks.ask: the words how many arrangements light up

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about packing figs.
<bookmark mark='farm'/>{{NAME_1}} and {{NAME_3}} grow figs on their farm.
<bookmark mark='boxes'/>{{NAME_1}} wants twelve figs in each box, and {{NAME_3}} wants seven figs in each box.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The figs in a box must sit in a rectangle. How many arrangements are possible?

beats.on_screen: the boxes and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a box of figs with its rows drawn across and its columns drawn down; the words rows × columns = figs

marks.rows: the rows are drawn across and the columns are drawn down
marks.equal: every row shows the same number of figs
marks.rule: the words rows × columns = figs are written

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Rows go across, and columns go down.
<bookmark mark='equal'/>In a rectangle of figs, every row has the same number of figs.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The number of rows times the number of columns gives the number of figs.

beats.on_screen: Given: 12 figs ({{NAME_1}}), 7 figs ({{NAME_3}}), each in a rectangle

marks.given: the two numbers of figs are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, twelve figs for {{NAME_1}} and seven figs for {{NAME_3}}, each laid in a rectangle.

beats.on_screen: To find: every rectangle each heap can make

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find every rectangle that each heap of figs can make.

beats.on_screen: 12 figs: 12 × 1 = 12, 6 × 2 = 12, 4 × 3 = 12 drawn as three rectangles; a try of 5 rows of 2 leaves 2 figs over and is crossed out

marks.twelve: the first line for twelve figs is written
marks.fits: the three exact rectangles are drawn in teal
marks.five: the try of five rows leaves two figs over and is crossed out
marks.side: a rectangle turned sideways is drawn on top of the first and merges with it

narration: <bookmark mark='twelve'/>Step one, try rows for twelve figs, because rows times columns must give twelve.
<bookmark mark='fits'/>One row of twelve, two rows of six and three rows of four all fit exactly.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five rows would leave two figs over, so only exact fits count.
<bookmark mark='side'/>A rectangle turned sideways is the same arrangement, so it is not counted twice.

beats.on_screen: 7 figs: 7 × 1 = 7 in one row; tries of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 rows leave figs over and are crossed out

marks.seven: the line for seven figs is written
marks.one: one row of seven figs is drawn in teal
marks.others: the tries of two to six rows leave figs over and are crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step two, try rows for seven figs, because rows times columns must give seven.
<bookmark mark='one'/>One row of seven fits exactly, which is seven times one.
<bookmark mark='others'/>Two, three, four, five or six rows each leave some figs over.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 12 figs make 3 arrangements, 7 figs make 1 arrangement

marks.unit: the words three arrangements and one arrangement light up

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Twelve figs make three rectangles, and seven figs make only one.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>That is three arrangements of twelve figs and one arrangement of seven figs.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: 7 figs cannot make a rectangle, crossed out; one row of 7 figs outlined as a rectangle 7 wide and 1 tall

marks.doubt: Keeko's doubt appears in a bubble
marks.row: one row of seven figs is outlined as a rectangle

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks seven figs cannot make a rectangle at all.
<bookmark mark='row'/>But look at one row of seven figs. It is a rectangle, seven figs wide and one fig tall.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A rectangle may be only one fig tall, so seven figs make exactly one rectangle.
